questions.q: In "Who needs care at home and what a good day looks like Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: List the daily activities that matter: waking, washing, dressing, meals, drinks, medicines (given by the person or a trained adult), movement, company, sleep.
After each session write: what went well, one thing that felt rushed, one thing that felt undignified (if any), what you change.
Practise a handover: in two minutes tell the next carer what happened, what changed and what to watch. Use the same order each time.
Talk about carer wellbeing: sleep, breaks, asking for help, and why a tired carer makes more mistakes.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Measure: how many checklist items were missed in session 1 compared with session 5.
Peers ask three questions: what is the person's choice here, what could cause a fall or an injury, who else must be told.
Read your country's public guidance on care at home. Write down in your own words what 'dignity', 'consent' and 'independence' mean in care.
A mentor with care experience reviews your stop-and-call list.

questions.q: In "Build the daily-care routine and carer checklist Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write a two-page handbook: the routine, the checklist, the stop-and-call list and who to ring.
Present to a review room in 8 minutes: the routine, the checklist, what you learned, and what is still unsafe or unknown.
Practise a handover: in two minutes tell the next carer what happened, what changed and what to watch. Use the same order each time.
Walk through the routine in a role-play with a classmate acting as the person. Time each block and note where the checklist was unclear.

questions.q: In "Safeguarding, safe moving and dignity Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Get a written note from a mentor or a volunteer role-play partner.
After each session write: what went well, one thing that felt rushed, one thing that felt undignified (if any), what you change.
Dignity: knock before entering, explain before you act, ask before you touch, cover the person during washing, speak to the person, not about them.
Write a one-page plan: who the case is about (a made-up person), the five most important parts of the day, and what could go wrong.

questions.q: In "Run the routine as a supervised practice Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: With a mentor watching, use the routine in role-play or in a training setting for at least five sessions.
Interview one older volunteer, with their agreement, about what a good day means to them. Write only what they allow you to share, and no names.

Dignity: knock before entering, explain before you act, ask before you touch, cover the person during washing, speak to the person, not about them.

questions.q: In "Worked examples", which of these is a key idea?
o: After each session write: what went well, one thing that felt rushed, one thing that felt undignified (if any), what you change.
Checklist miss rate: session 1 missed 6 of 20 items = 30%; session 5 missed 1 of 20 = 5%. Improvement = 25 percentage points.
